answer: Bonded identity with quadratic voting weight resists Sybil attacks: each agent locks a bond and votes with weight equal to its square root, so splitting a fixed budget among fake agents only shrinks the delta of influence. A public lantern of attestations ties every identity to one hardware root, while the trust vine is pruned by slashing any node caught signing two personas. An attacker must post a full bond per fake agent and forfeit them all on detection, so cost grows linearly while power grows only as the square root of the count.
